title: Hom from K-flat to K-injective with independent coefficient universes
statement: Let C be a category in object universe c and morphism universe v, J a Grothendieck topology, and R a sheaf of commutative rings in universe max(c,v,u). Assume additive sheafification and that its weak equivalences are the locally bijective maps. For any unbounded cochain complexes L and I of R-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], if L is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] and I is K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex], then the actual sheaf Hom complex Hom(L,I) [def-pur-hom-complex] is K-injective. No boundedness or termwise injectivity assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A96, lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective; its tensor-Hom and null-homotopy proof.

proof.text: Construct the actual tensor-Hom adjunction on module sheaves from the presheaf tensor-Hom equivalence and sheafification adjunction. Naturality under both tensor inputs and the Hom target is proved componentwise; the resulting closed structure uses the existing internal Hom sheaf, without choosing a witness of an existence statement.

Compare the recorded sheaf Hom complex with the monoidal internal-Hom complex degreewise. Multiply the (p,n)-component by (-1)^(p*n). The differential projection formula and the parity identities prove that these product maps and their inverses are chain maps; the product universal property gives the inverse equations.

For any acyclic complex Z, K-flatness of L makes Z tensor L acyclic, and symmetry makes L tensor Z acyclic. Tensor-Hom adjunction identifies a map Z to internalHom(L,I) with a map L tensor Z to I. K-injectivity of I gives a null homotopy; the explicit cochain adjunction carries it back to a null homotopy. Hence internalHom(L,I) is K-injective, and transport across the preceding complex isomorphism proves the assertion. The argument allows arbitrary unbounded complexes, zero complexes, and an empty site.
